INSTALL-UX-001.title: Installs have real progress, failure recovery, and a receipt
INSTALL-UX-001.summary: Pack install is bounded and honest: real progress, cancel/retry/resume, a receipt, and an explicit decision on pre-archived bundles.
INSTALL-UX-001.notes: Transport hardening is done (PACK-DL-ALLOWLIST-001). Implemented 2026-10-15: `engine-progress` carries a measured fetch percent from the pinned `PackEntry.size_bytes`, `verify`/unpack are named as unmeasurable rather than faked, cancel is honoured at chunk/redirect/phase boundaries (`cancel_pack_install` + `INSTALL_CANCEL`), and an `InstallReceipt` (pack/version/source host/sha256/size/capabilities) reaches the UI with Cancel and Retry. The second slice the same day closed both disclosed gaps: `lts_langpack::archive::install_with_cancel` takes a hook consulted per archive entry and again before the store is touched, and because extraction is staging-then-rename an abort leaves no version directory and never moves the `current` pointer; a cancelled transfer keeps its bytes in `partial-<key>.part` beside a sidecar naming url/sha256/size, so a retry sends `Range: bytes=<n>-`, adopts the prefix only on a `206`, and still checks the completed file against the pinned size and SHA-256 before the pack gate sees it — a `200` answer, a corrupt or foreign sidecar, or an oversized part restarts from zero. `install_from_catalog_report` refuses an install that cannot fit (free space from `statvfs` on unix, skipped rather than guessed elsewhere) and names a disk that fills during unpack. The renderer offers Cancel during fetch/verify/install and its copy now says a retry continues where it stopped. Still open and owner-gated: the measured timing half of issue #1 item I05 (fresh-artifact install and resume timed separately on the tiers `PERF-002` freezes) needs a published artifact, and the pre-archived-bundle question stays an owner decision. Evidence: state/evidence/INSTALL-UX-001/ENGINE-SLICE-2026-10-15.md, state/evidence/INSTALL-UX-001/RESUME-CANCEL-PREFLIGHT-2026-10-15.md. JA-KANJI-DECOMP-UI-001.notes: Closed 2026-10-18 with the rule written down in apps/desktop/src/kanji-decomposition.ts and the K-16 section of docs/03_CURRICULUM_AND_MASTERY.md rather than inferred from the render; App.tsx:2868-2871 derives it and App.tsx:3188-3209 renders it. Opened 2026-10-16 from the measured learner-facing cost of option A (recorded before it was chosen): radical-list min/max/mean is 1/7/2.45; 22 of 84 cards present the character as its own sole element; 62 of 84 list nested elements; 23 of 84 contain the non-CJK stand-ins `ノ ハ ヨ |` that KRADFILE uses for strokes with no standalone glyph (the last is FULLWIDTH VERTICAL LINE U+FF5C, not an ASCII pipe). Re-measured after implementation: 22 whole, 1 strokes-only (八 -> [ハ]), 61 with real parts (8 single-element, 53 multi-element; 22 of those also carry strokes). 5 cards list the character among other elements (風 口 足 見 行) and those self-references are dropped. Nesting is framed in the multi-element sentence instead of computed per card: 話 lists 言/口/舌, and neither 言 nor 舌 is a card, so a cross-card lookup would have missed the acceptance example.

PACK-UPDATE-UX-001.title: A newer catalogue version of an installed pack is offered as an update
PACK-UPDATE-UX-001.summary: One installed-pack record feeds Home, the practice hub and the onboarding wizard, so a pack the catalogue lists at a different version is shown with both versions plus an update control wherever the learner already is.
PACK-UPDATE-UX-001.notes: Implemented 2026-10-17. `installedPacks: string[]` is gone from App.tsx and from OnboardingProps: the single record is `installed: InstalledPack[]` (App.tsx:320) filled by `refreshInstalled()` (App.tsx:931-942), which returns the records it read or null when the read failed and sets `installedUnknown` so the wizard still offers retry and Skip for now. Boot gained its own `catalog_packs` read in a separate try/catch (App.tsx:849-858) because `catalog` is otherwise empty during the wizard. The derived block (App.tsx:2840-2867) joins `available_version` onto each wizard row from `catalog` and derives `packUpdates` purely from entries whose non-null `installed_version` differs from `version`, so Home, the hub and Settings read one derivation. `updateFromCatalog(id)` (App.tsx:947-972) calls the same `install_catalog_pack` command Settings uses, then re-reads installed packs and the catalogue; `install(id)` re-checks through `refreshInstalled()` instead of fabricating a record, because `install_pack` returns a PackCandidate with no version (lib.rs:422-432) while `import_pack` (lib.rs:523) returns the full record. The wizard renders both versions in three states (stale, matching, no listed version) and the update control is a sibling of the untouched Install/Installed button; Continue is never disabled for a version mismatch. Learner copy never says newer or latest and never promises progress survives an update. Measured on GamingPC: `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 errors; `npx vitest run` 29 files / 253 tests (baseline 29 / 246), per-file counts 15->18 onboarding, 25->26 home, 3->4 hub, 10->10 a11y; `tools/audit_learner_copy.py` findings: 0. Criterion 2 rests on engine code unchanged here: the download re-verifies against the pin (packs.rs:846-900) and `crates/langpack/tests/media_upgrade.rs:161` keeps the previous version for rollback. `scripts/smoke-desktop.sh` stays owner-side because 127.0.0.1:1420 is held by the owner's running app.

JA-FUNCTION-WORD-LOOKUP-001.title: Tap-lookup resolves closed-class words to their correct sense
JA-FUNCTION-WORD-LOOKUP-001.summary: Reading tap-lookup offers the wrong sense for function words: the topic particle は surfaces the tooth noun and に surfaces 'two', because the pack lexicon has no particle entries; closed-class spans need correctly sourced lexicon entries plus a reading-consistency check.
JA-FUNCTION-WORD-LOOKUP-001.notes: Found 2026-10-21 by the owner's sweep (packet section 2 item 4 leg 2, finding S-3): the lookup panel under 「わたしの なまえは タナカです。」 listed 'は ha — tooth'. Pack data confirms lexicon/health4.jsonl carries は/tooth as the only は entry and lexicon/numbers has に/two, while particles live only as grammar concepts (ja.grammar.particle.*), invisible to the lexicon-driven panel; the なまえ/まえ half of the check PASSED (K-80 span fix holds on the real surface). Fix is pack content (add sourced particle entries, jmdict-simplified covers them, draft posture unchanged) plus a repo-side check that flags any story-sentence span whose entry conflicts with the sentence's declared reading (surface は vs reading wa at that span) or resolves to no entry. Whether this rides REL-001 or lands at 1.0.x is an owner scope call.

IME-TOGGLE-UX-001.notes: Captured from the owner's item-7 sweep pass (packet section 2 item 7, 'that worked perfectly'): key-command toggle + corner bubble flippable by click. Clarified same day: (1) 'any window' = any window inside the OLLP program - app-chrome bubble, no tray/global-shortcut requirement; (2) 'this works for any language not just japanese. it wouldn't make sense to have 日本語 if you're learning russian' - the bubble label and the keyboard itself are resolved from the ACTIVE pack's declared capability + mapping data; a non-kana pack shows no bubble and no keyboard (ties to SETTINGS-PACK-CAPABILITY-001). Phase 1's kana converter is the instance; generalizing means pack-declared mapping assets + a converter, never a language branch in engine or UI; the per-profile 'kana-keyboard' setting key gets renamed at implementation. Screen-reader announcement of mode changes follows A11Y-FLOW-001 semantics.
